title: The Disk Alert That Won't Stop
symptom: The root filesystem alert has been firing for an hour. A teammate already cleared /tmp — no change. Writes are starting to fail.

goals.description: The root filesystem is below 80% used
The worker service is still running

evidence.description: what is actually using the space

options: The worker's debug log grew without limit — and because the worker holds it open, deleting the file alone frees nothing
Old Docker images filled the disk
Millions of small temp files in /tmp

debrief: du walked the tree to /var/log/worker/debug.log: a debug-level log that nobody turned off. Truncating it frees the space immediately even though the worker keeps it open. If you rm'd it instead, df didn't move — the kernel only frees blocks when the last open handle closes, which is why 'lsof +L1' and restarting the worker were needed (linux-incident-002 is this exact trap). Permanent fixes: set the worker back to info-level logging, add logrotate, and alert at 80% instead of discovering it at 97%.
